http://en.people.cn/n3/2026/0806/c90000-.text: Home Opinion PD Voice Politics Foreign Affairs Business World We Are China Society Culture Sci-Tech Video Photo Sports Travel Military Life Exclusive Specials Languages Chinese Japanese French Spanish Russian Arabic Korean German Portuguese Swahili Italian Kazakh Thai Malay Greek Vietnamese Urdu Hindi Archive "Furnace city" emerges as "coolcation" magnet for global travelers CHONGQING, Aug. 6 (Xinhua) -- Despite outdoor temperatures nearing 40 degrees Celsius in southwest China's Chongqing Municipality, Australian tourist Roy Rostand was enjoying hotpot at a restaurant without air conditioning, apparently feeling no discomfort from the summer heat. The answer to his comfort lies in the restaurant's unlikely location. This hotpot restaurant, named Underground City, is hidden inside a former air-raid shelter, one of the city's distinctive spaces offering natural coolness. "It's amazing that the restaurant stays so cool even in scorching summer heat," Rostand said. "Chongqing has given me the chance to experience something I can't find in Australia." Chongqing has long been dubbed one of China's "furnace cities" for its sweltering, humid summers. In July alone, the city endured 26 consecutive days of high heat, with temperatures breaching 40 degrees Celsius for a full week and topping out at a scorching 41.6 degrees. The blazing heat, however, has failed to dampen the enthusiasm of global travelers. According to the Chongqing General Station of Exit and Entry Frontier Inspection, more than 610,000 inbound and outbound trips by foreign nationals were recorded at Chongqing Jiangbei International Airport in the first half of the year, marking an 86-percent surge year on year. The top five source countries were Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Vietnam and Indonesia. European travelers proved to be a standout growth driver. Data from Trip.com shows that as of July 21, inbound travel bookings from Europe to Chongqing for this summer season climbed by over 40 percent year on year, while scenic spot ticket orders surged by 214.7 percent and activity-based bookings rocketed by a staggering 6,900 percent. Thanks to China's visa-free policies and other travel facilitation measures, Chongqing is rapidly gaining traction as a go-to "coolcation" hotspot for international visitors. Creative cool-off spaces, diverse travel experiences and comprehensive summer services have all contributed to its rising appeal. UNDERGROUND COOL Chongqing's summer cooling secrets were first found underground. Since the late 1930s, the city has carved thousands of air-raid shelters into its mountainous terrain. Once serving as sanctuaries for civilians during the Chinese People's War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression, these spaces have now been repurposed as hotpot restaurants, tea houses and venues for Sichuan Opera performances, providing both refreshing coolness and preserving the city's living memories. "The temperature inside the shelters remains around 25 degrees Celsius all year round, making them natural cool retreats," explained Wang Jing, marketing director of Underground City. "We serve more than 300 tables a day on weekends," she added. "Right now, about one in every six diners is from overseas. And we're seeing more and more visitors from Southeast Asia and Europe." Annika, a tourist from Germany, revealed that the restaurant has gone viral on overseas social media platforms. "We were attracted not only by this unique way of escaping the summer heat, but also by the opportunity to dine in a place filled with history and culture," she said. CHASING CHILL On August 1, Chongqing issued an orange heat alert. At a water park in its Fuling District, 10 tonnes of industrial ice were dumped directly into the wave pool. Half-submerged in the refreshing water, visitors could splash around or even play mahjong at custom-made tables in the pool. This unique summer cooling scene has attracted coverage from mainstream media in countries including Russia and Canada, with overseas outlets reportedly dubbing it the most intriguing summer spectacle in China this year. At Chongqing Xingrui international travel service, inquiries from cross-border travelers hailing from hot and humid regions such as Vietnam, Laos and Indonesia have risen notably in recent weeks. Peng Hengcong, head of the travel agency, said they have rolled out themed tour products, including "cool retreats in the mountains" and "gorge rapids adventures," tailored to overseas visitors seeking summer cooling experiences. These products cover areas with higher altitudes or rich water systems in Chongqing, with the highlight being a "23Â°C summer" experience. Luo Zibai, an expert with the China Tourism Academy, believes that Chongqing's sustained popularity among travelers lies in its ability to fully leverage its distinctive strengths and develop differentiated tourism products that offer a broad spectrum of experiences. URBAN REFUGE Chongqing is weaving a citywide "cooling network" -- ranging from shopping malls to public facilities, and from indoor spaces to outdoor areas. At a shopping mall called The Ring in the city, visitors are greeted not by endless rows of shops, but by a lush indoor rainforest. With misting systems and carefully designed lighting, the mall keeps the temperature at about 21 degrees Celsius, creating a cool, dreamy summer escape. "I like Chongqing a lot because it has its own character," said Bilal Badri, who was visiting from the Netherlands. "The way nature and the city's landscape blend together here is just perfect." The cool experience extends beyond the mall. In the Mountain City Alley historic district, a 400-meter-long pedestrian walkway has been transformed into a "cooling corridor," where misting systems and shaded areas reduce the perceived temperature by 3 to 5 degrees Celsius. In addition, since July 8, Chongqing's rail transit system has set up cooling zones in 158 metro stations, offering free air-conditioned spaces and heat-relief supplies to residents and tourists alike. "Chongqing's creative and thoughtful ways to help people beat the summer heat are impressive. It's really interesting to discover these unique experiences," said Alexandra, a Romanian tourist. "This time I didn't stay long enough to explore more of the city, and I'm planning to come back in the near future." West AP AP X Story Stream recent articles Video: Global Warming Lorem Ipsum Dolor Sit ... Article: Global Warming Lorem Ipsum Dolor Sit ... Article: Global Warming Lorem Ipsum Dolor Sit ... Video: Global Warming Lorem Ipsum Dolor Sit ... “Ladies and Gentlemen, Hungary is back.” This declaration by Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi, the Central European nation’s new Defense Minister, quickly became the running motto last week at the Equilibrium Institute’s Budapest Energy and Security Talks (BEST), at which this author was in attendance. It was a sentiment defense policymakers from both sides of the Atlantic have longed to hear. At the forefront of the newly elected Prime Minister Peter Magyar’s administration is the message that it will bring Hungary’s foreign policy into alignment with the rest of Europe. The BEST forum functioned as a presentation of the new government’s security policies to the rest of the world. Geopolitical experts, military officers, business leaders, and policymakers from across Europe and the U.S. debated and discussed issues concerning energy strategy, AI development, and state infrastructural cybersecurity. Discourse centered on building a common outlook to be shared by Washington, Budapest, and their common allies. What was clear throughout the various panels was the new administration’s intention to firmly reassert Hungary as a member of the pro-NATO camp. Realization of his vision is contingent upon Magyar’s successful cultivation of Budapest’s relationship with Washington. The liaison between Hungary and NATO has been complex for several years. Hungarians never stopped their contribution to the alliance nor hesitated to provide aid to Ukraine’s fleeing people when they were able. From leading the aerial defense of the Baltics, to providing aid and shelter, often in their own homes, to the millions of Ukrainian war refugees, the Hungarian people and armed forces more than did their part. The nation has kept to its commitment to spend over two percent of its GDP towards NATO, according to the Atlantic Council. The war played a noticeable role in Hungarians’ voting decisions as well, with many seeing parallels to the Soviet invasion of 1956. Politically however, tensions boiled. Examples include Orban delaying Sweden and Finland’s accession to NATO and having constant spats with Kyiv over allegations of maltreatment of Ukraine’s Hungarian minority community. Russian oil exports were a constant specter with Kyiv seeking to halt their facilitation to bleed Putin’s war chest. Meanwhile, Orban accused Ukrainian President Zelenskyy of endangering Hungarian energy stability. Chinese Belt and Road investments in telecommunications development, manufacturing and logistics, and AI research and development agreements are firmly entrenched and even accompanied by security agreements between Beijing and Budapest. Stranger episodes entail Hungarian authorities detaining Ukrainian money trucks and claims of Ukrainian threats against Orban’s family. The chaotic portfolio of the nation’s foreign affairs, along with the endemic accusations of corruption and nepotism, were notable factors in Hungarians’ election decisions. The biggest loser of this election is Putin. The last major impediment to European unity on providing support to NATO and Ukraine has ended. At the same time, President Trump has signaled a shift of sympathy from Putin towards Kyiv due to its recent battlefield progress, most notably with permission to build Patriot Missile systems. Putin faces a united Europe; one with an appetite to develop military capabilities and industrial production. Orban’s departure does not signal that the West’s previous issues are resolved. One of the first actions of the new Prime Minister was to meet President Zelenskyy over the issue of protecting minority Hungarians in Ukraine’s Transcarpathia region. Hungary also remains heavily reliant on direct Russian energy sources, as does the rest of Europe through a loophole of facilitating it through Türkiye. Magyar acknowledges the potential dangers of relations with China and seeks limits, but does not call for Beijing’s departure, if he can even do so. The extent of the danger in Orban’s dealings with Beijing is still being investigated. Facing such daunting challenges, Hungary and its allies need each other more than ever. To its credit, Magyar’s cabinet did demonstrate at the conference a clear command of the issues Budapest needs to address in order to secure its position with NATO. The joint development of regional defense industrial capacity, strengthening collective cybersecurity and AI development, and pursing energy autonomy are all critical. On these issues they find common ground with President Trump and his demands that Europe take more responsibility for its own self-defense. At the summit however, a focus on “European sovereignty” was occasionally pondered, in which Europe would have the capacity to operate without acting in concert with the U.S. Such thoughts are not without cause. President Trump’s criticisms of European defense shortcomings, contentions with Ukraine, and previous statements of affinity with Putin have raised European questions about the need for greater autonomy. Any distance the Prime Minister has with Washington at the moment should not come as a surprise given Trump’s affinity with Magyar’s political rival. Vice President J.D. Vance even campaigned for Orban during Hungary’s election season. On fair balance, “keeping America engaged with Europe” was another common line at the summit. A notable proponent was Turkish Deputy Foreign Minister Levent Gümrükçü, who acknowledged the history of unequal burden sharing upon the United States concerning Europe’s defense. His comments come after Trump stated his intent to lift sanctions against Türkiye’s acquisition of F-35 jets stemming from the purchase of the Russian S-400 air defense system at the NATO Summit in Ankara earlier this month. The underlying tension that continues to appear amidst these events is the issue of lingering mistrust between western nations. This proves that NATO’s political alignment challenges did not end with the Orban administration’s departure. The overwhelming consensus of the Budapest conference’s attendees was that “the West is stronger together.” Left unaddressed however, the vestiges of division could grow and overtake them. While Europe must develop domestic capacities to avoid the past mistake of being completely reliant on the Americans, total autonomy is neither feasible nor even desirable. For one, European love of regulation has long hampered its ability to innovate in terms of defense capability. The willingness to relax standards was a hotly debated topic at the conference, signaling a continued need for complementary American ingenuity both in cyber and industrial developments. While Ukraine’s heroic defense of its homeland from Russia has resulted in cosmic leaps of drone capability, it alone is not enough to meet Europe’s needs. American defense industrial manufacturing remains a dominant force in global military affairs. It’s utilization in Europe’s rearmament is critical from a strategic disposition, specifically to offer NATO’s member militaries common operating platforms. U.S. maintenance of European relations is needed to maintain its agency on the continent. As the lack of progress in the Iran conflict demonstrates, little of lasting worth is accomplished without cooperation among allies. If Prime Minister Magyar intends to prove that “Hungary is back” politically in NATO, he’ll need to ensure that he does not repeat a mistake that his predecessor made: driving away allies, both domestic and international. The European Union and the U.S. made numerous errors in the manner of their engagements with the Orban administration, which arguably encouraged closer relations with Moscow and Beijing. Meanwhile, Orban’s folly was bringing his nation too close to the eastern powers. This created political isolation at home and abroad, widening the trust gap between Budapest and its strategic defense allies. Beyond these contentions, the bigger security issues the U.S. and Europe need to address are too great for any to face alone. For both Hungary and Europe, true independence is contingent on a strong defense pact with America. For the U.S., continued global agency relies on strong allies. Despite the presence of some disputes, the dominant message of the Budapest conference was for Europe and the U.S. to stand together firmly in NATO. That sentiment must guide policymaking on both sides of the alliance’s namesake ocean. Logan C. West is a doctoral student of statecraft and strategy at the Institute of World Politics in Washington D.C. and an alumnus of the Hungary Foundation’s Budapest Fellowship Program. https://telex.hu/after/2026/09/10/jakab-.text: Menü Kereső A kurzusfilmeknél azért több embert érdekel, ha Ember Márk csókolózik valakivel After Szente Katica A Telex hatodik születésnapján Jakab Juli, Kövesi Zsombor és Georgita Máté Dezső színészekkel arról beszélgettünk , hogyan látják a színház és film jövőjét a kormányváltás után. Szóba került, hogy áll a filmszakma reformja, és az is, hogy miért zavarja a színészeket, hogy a színház az elit hóbortja lett. Vendégeink kifejtették azt is, szerintük hogyan lehetne párbeszédet kezdeményezni abban a szakmában, amit megosztott a NER tizenhat éve. „A filmszakma nagyon erősen megmozdult, számomra fontos, hogy ebben a dramaturgoknak és forgatókönyvíróknak is lett szerepe, erős ambíciók vannak arra, hogy legyen egy érdekvédelem, hogy ismét biztonságos legyen a filmfinanszírozás” – mesélte Jakab Juli, aki egyébként forgatókönyv-fejlesztőként is dolgozott a Filmalapnál, és már a Telex stúdiójában is beszélt Káel Csaba egykori filmügyi kormánybiztos támogatási rendszeréről. Jakab Juli szerint az pozitív hozadéka a mostanában készült magyar romantikus vígjátékoknak és musicaleknek, hogy az emberek elmennek a mozikba, és nem várják meg, amíg egy magyar film felkerül streamingre. Úgy fogalmazott, jó az a felismerés, hogy a történelmi kurzusfilmeknél több embert érdekel, ha Ember Márk csókolózik valakivel. Azért hozzátette, hogy szerinte volt olyan magyar film, például a Legénybúcsú , ahol a vezető alkotók tisztelhették volna jobban magukat, a többi stábtagot és a nézőket annál, ahogy azt a filmjükben tették. Georgita Máté Dezső, akit A király című sorozatból ismerhetett meg a szélesebb közönség, DanteCasino néven alapított a barátaival egy társulatot, ahol középiskolásoknak is tartanak színjátszó szakkört, mert fontos számukra, hogy a társadalom széles köreinek is elérhető legyen a színház. „Van egy mesedarabunk a feleségemmel, sokat járunk falvakba, ahol olyan közönségnek játszunk, amely sosem juthatott el színházba, ezek mindig csodálatos reakciók” – mondta. Ezzel Kövesi Zsombor is egyetértett, aki szerint színészként nem olyan közönségnek szeretne játszani, amelynek tagjai egyébként is műveltek és jártasak a kultúrában, hanem szeretné megismertetni ezt a világot egy szélesebb réteggel. „Jó lenne, ha a színház olyan lenne, mint a kenyér” – mondta Kövesi. A színész arról is mesélt, hogy fenyegette már őt a kiégés, hiszen nincsenek hétvégéi, reggeltől estig próbákon és előadásokon játszik, de az olyan filmek után, mint a Marty Supreme vagy az Egyik csata a másik után , visszatér a kedve a hivatásához. „A magyar filmeknél úgy érzem, hogy egysíkú karaktereket kell bemutatni, nekem is azt mondják általában, hogy úgy játsszak, ami ösztönös, de akkor az Kövesi Zsombor-os lesz. Hiányolom a kraftot a magyar filmes szerepekből” – tette hozzá a színész. Az adásban szóba kerül még: Miért nem bánta meg Kövesi Zsombor, hogy elvállalta Káel Csaba Magyar menyegzőjében az egyik főszerepet? Jakab Juli szerint miért fűződik majd szomorú időszak Káel Csaba nevéhez? Miért baj, hogy rendszeresen ugyanazokat a színészeket szerepeltetik filmekben a készítők? Kövess minket Facebookon is! Követem! Friss az Afteren

https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/10/28/magy.text: Menü Kereső Ránk számíthattok! 3000 új támogatót keresünk Csatlakozom Magyar Péter: A motoros roller külön járműkategória lesz a KRESZ-ben, és tilos lesz alkoholos befolyásoltság esetén használni Belföld frissítve Vida Benjámin Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „A kormány javaslata szerint a motoros roller külön járműkategória lesz a KRESZ-ben, és speciális szabályok vonatkoznak majd rá: tilos lesz alkoholos befolyásoltság esetén használni, tilos lesz rajta második személyt szállítani. A nagy teljesítményű elektromos rollerek esetében minden esetben tilos lesz a járda használata, kis teljesítményű elektromos rollerek esetében is csak akkor lesz megengedett, ha nincs semmilyen más alternatív lehetőség, például kerékpárút” – jelentette be Magyar Péter miniszterelnök a szerdai Facebook-videójában . A kormányfő közölte, hogy a KRESZ módosításáról és szigorításáról szóló rendeletet a kihirdetése előtt még egyszer társadalmi vitára bocsátják. A kormány által összeállított javaslat szerint ezentúl két jármű-kategóriába sorolják az elektromos rollereket a teljesítményük alapján. Kis teljesítményű rollernek számítanak azok, amelyek legfeljebb 25 km/h-s sebességre képesek. Ezek használatának 14 év lesz az alsó korhatára, és 18 éves korig kötelező lesz majd a fejvédő használata mindenkinek. Nagy teljesítményű motoros roller kategóriába tartozik majd minden eszköz, amelynek 25 km/h-nál magasabb a maximális sebessége. Ezeket 16 éven felül lehet majd használni, de legalább AM kategóriás, tehát segédmotorokhoz és robogókhoz szükséges jogosítvány megszerzéséhez lesz kötve, és a bukósisak használata mindenki számára kötelező lesz. A nagy teljesítményű motoros rollerek esetében a maximális sebesség 40 km/h lesz. A bérelhető elektromos rollerek esetében 20 km/h-ban lesz maximalizálva a végsebesség. Magyar Péter arról is beszélt a videóban, hogy az elmúlt években drámaian nőtt az elektromos rollerek használatával összefüggő balesetek száma. A miniszterelnök azt mondta, nem abból indultak ki, hogy a tiltás mindent megold. „Az elektromos roller nem rossz dolog, sőt, a megjelenése hatékonyabbá és fenntarthatóbbá teszi a közlekedést” – fogalmazott. Magyar szerint nehéz kérdés volt, hogy hol húzzák meg a határokat, és milyen szabályokat vezessenek be. Ezért nyáron a kormány közlekedésbiztonsági felmérést indított , amit végül több mint 360 ezren töltöttek ki . A kormányfő azt is közölte, hogy ugyanezekről a kérdésekről készült egy reprezentatív közvélemény-kutatás is. Magyar szerint mind a társadalmi párbeszédben, mind a reprezentatív kutatásban résztvevők, mind a szakemberek egyetértettek abban, hogy az elektromos rollerek szabályozásának a lehető leghamarabb meg kell történnie. https://hotnews.ro/unul-dintre-oficialii.text: O bombă amplasată într-un autoturism a rănit vineri la Moscova un fost purtător de cuvânt al fostului premier ucrainean Mikola Azarov, cunoscut pentru pozițiile sale proruse, au anunțat anchetatorii ruși, citați de Reuters . Este al doilea incident de acest fel produs în țară în decurs de două zile. Serghei Zavorotnii, care a fost cândva unul dintre principalii colaboratori ai lui Mikola Azarov – prim-ministru al Ucrainei în perioada 2010-2014 -, a fost spitalizat după ce mașina pe care o conducea a explodat pe o stradă din Certanovo, un cartier al capitalei ruse, potrivit comunicatului anchetatorilor. Moscova a acuzat Ucraina pentru asasinatele anterioare ale unor înalți oficiali militari și ale unor persoane cu legături cu Rusia. Kievul nu a făcut deocamdată niciun comentariu privind noul incident. Postul de televiziune Ren TV și canalul de Telegram 112 au relatat că Zavorotnii și-ar fi pierdut brațul stâng în urma atacului și că se afla în spital, suferind de comoție cerebrală, coaste fracturate și alte răni. Canalul de Telegram Baza a publicat o fotografie cu un autoturism negru, cu patru uși, având parbrizul, portierele și bara de protecție din față distruse, pe o stradă din oraș. Бывший советник экс-премьера Украины Николая Азарова Сергей Заворотный в результате взрыва лишился левой руки и получил тяжелые травмы головы и тяжелые переломы ног . Его ввели в состоянии искуственной комы. Взрыв прогремел сегодня около 10:20 на Кировоградской улице в Москве. Бомба была заложена под днище машины и сработала во время движения. Взрывной волной Завротного выкинуло на улицу, а машина еще проехала 500 м Comitetul de Investigații al Rusiei, instituția care se ocupă de infracțiunile grave, a anunțat că investighează incidentul. Azarov, fostul șef al lui Zavorotnîi, a fugit în Rusia în 2014 , când protestele de stradă din Ucraina, cunoscute ulterior sub numele de Revoluția Maidanului, au dus la înlăturarea președintelui prorus Viktor Ianukovici, după ce acesta renunțase la angajamentul de a dezvolta relații mai strânse cu Uniunea Europeană. Azarov a declarat vineri agenției de presă de stat ruse TASS că nu deține nicio informație despre atentatul cu bombă asupra mașinii, cu excepția faptului că Zavorotnii a supraviețuit. Explozia este cel mai recent incident dintr-o serie de presupuse tentative de asasinat comise pe teritoriul Rusiei. Joi, un membru al armatei ruse a fost ucis într-un atentat cu bombă asupra unui autoturism la Sankt Petersburg. În unele cazuri, surse ucrainene și-au revendicat responsabilitatea, în timp ce în altele au negat orice implicare. Kievul nu a comentat atacul de joi. Azarov și Ianukovici au fugit în Rusia după ce peste 100 de manifestanți au fost uciși în capitala Ucrainei, Kiev, în timpul intervenției forțelor de securitate împotriva protestelor de amploare. În 2019, un tribunal ucrainean l-a condamnat în lipsă pe Ianukovici la 13 ani de închisoare pentru trădare, iar Kievul a impus ulterior sancțiuni împotriva acestuia și a lui Azarov. După ce s-a mutat în Rusia în 2014, Zavorotnii a început să lucreze ca analist și comentator politic, publicând articole în care critica structurile de securitate ale Ucrainei.
